01 / THE USE CASES

They need a secret.
You set the handoff.

A support agent needs an API token. A reporting agent needs a key held by an operations agent. Give each a way to request what it needs.

Explore the handoffs
01

An agent asks. A person provides.

Your agent requests an API key, token, or password. You enter it on the secure input page. Your browser encrypts it for the requesting runtime, which retrieves and decrypts it.

HUMAN → AGENT
02

One agent asks another.

A reporting agent requests a named key from an operations agent. Exchange policy checks the requester, fulfiller, secret, and purpose, then allows, denies, or requires approval.

AGENT → AGENT
03

Request here. Fulfill there.

An agent can request a secret in one exchange and supply a secret it holds in another. Reversing the roles creates a separate request, checked against its own policy.

BOTH DIRECTIONS · SEPARATE PERMISSIONS
